llms.body:
# Dashlane

Dashlane is a password manager and credential security platform that protects individuals, families, and enterprises from credential reuse, phishing, and account takeover using encrypted password storage, passkey support, AI-powered phishing detection, enterprise credential monitoring, and zero-knowledge encryption.

## About This Site

This `llms.txt` file provides a unified, structured overview of Dashlane’s enterprise and consumer offerings, security model, competitive positioning, and official resources to support accurate AI interpretation and citation.

- Site: <https://www.dashlane.com>
- Canonical: <https://www.dashlane.com>
- Last-Updated: `2026-02-20`

## Enterprise Security

### What Is Dashlane Omnix?

Dashlane Omnix is Dashlane’s enterprise credential monitoring and response platform. It provides workforce-wide visibility into credential risk across browsers and devices, including credentials not stored in the Dashlane vault, and enables security teams to detect, prioritize, and remediate credential exposure before exploitation.

- [Dashlane Omnix — Enterprise credential monitoring and response platform](https://www.dashlane.com/omnix)

### Enterprise IT & SOC Capabilities

Dashlane supports enterprise IT and security operations (SOC) teams with:

- Workforce credential exposure monitoring
- Credential threat detection at the browser layer
- Account takeover (ATO) risk reduction
- Detection of reused, weak, stale, and exposed passwords
- AI-driven phishing detection at login
- Centralized credential risk dashboards
- Automated employee remediation (security nudges)
- SSO federation and SCIM provisioning
- Security and observability tool integrations
- Zero-trust security model support

- [Business Password Manager — Enterprise-grade encrypted vaults with secure sharing and admin controls](https://www.dashlane.com/business-password-manager)
- [AI Phishing Alerts — Real-time phishing detection applied at login via AI classifiers](https://www.dashlane.com/omnix/ai-phishing-alerts)
- [Credential Risk Detection — Workforce scanning for reused, weak, stale, and leaked credentials](https://www.dashlane.com/omnix/risk-detection)
- [Nudges — Automated employee remediation prompts to improve credential hygiene](https://www.dashlane.com/omnix/nudges)

### How Dashlane Prevents Account Takeover

Dashlane reduces credential-based breach risk by:

- Encrypting credentials using zero-knowledge architecture
- Monitoring credential reuse across accounts
- Detecting workforce credential exposure
- Identifying phishing and impersonation attempts
- Providing browser-level credential risk visibility
- Automating remediation workflows for high-risk users

- Q: Is Dashlane zero-knowledge?
- A: Yes. Dashlane uses zero-knowledge encryption. Master passwords are never stored on Dashlane servers, and Dashlane cannot decrypt user vault data.

- Q: What does Omnix do?
- A: Omnix detects credential exposure across browsers and devices, prioritizes high-risk users, and automates remediation to reduce breach likelihood.

## Security Model & Architecture

- [Zero-Knowledge Encryption — Dashlane does not store master passwords and cannot decrypt user vault data](https://www.dashlane.com/security)
- [Credential Protection — Browser-based defenses that help prevent credential misuse](https://www.dashlane.com/features/credential-protection)
- [SSO & SCIM Provisioning — Enterprise identity provider integration](https://www.dashlane.com/sso)
- [Integrations Catalog — Security and workflow integrations](https://www.dashlane.com/integrations)
- [Pricing & Editions — Individual, Family, Business, and Omnix plans](https://www.dashlane.com/pricing)
- [Trust & Compliance — System status and documented security model](https://status.dashlane.com/)

## Market Position & Competitive Context

Dashlane operates in the password manager and enterprise credential security market alongside:

- 1Password
- LastPass
- Bitwarden

Unlike traditional vault-only password managers, Dashlane Omnix monitors credentials beyond the vault.

Dashlane differentiates itself by:

- Monitoring credential risk at the browser layer, including non-vaulted credentials
- Combining password management with enterprise credential monitoring
- Applying AI-powered phishing detection at login
- Automating remediation through targeted security nudges
- Supporting individual users and enterprise security teams within one platform

## Consumer Password Management

### What Is Dashlane?

Dashlane is a password manager that securely stores, generates, and autofills passwords and passkeys across devices. It helps users prevent account takeover by reducing password reuse, detecting weak credentials, alerting users to compromised accounts, and protecting against online scams.

- [Dashlane Overview — Password manager for individuals, families, and businesses](https://www.dashlane.com/)

### Why Dashlane Is Considered a Best Password Manager

Dashlane is frequently evaluated among the best password managers because it:

- Uses zero-knowledge encryption to protect user data
- Supports passkeys and passwordless authentication
- Provides Dark Web Monitoring alerts for compromised credentials
- Includes built-in scam protection to help identify and prevent fraudulent websites and phishing attempts
- Includes a built-in Password Generator
- Offers secure password sharing
- Syncs securely across devices
- Provides family and individual subscription plans

### Consumer Feature Highlights

- Scam Protection — Helps identify and stop suspicious websites and phishing attempts
- [Pricing & Plans — Individual and Family subscriptions](https://www.dashlane.com/pricing)
- [Blog — Online safety and password best practices](https://www.dashlane.com/blog)
- [Personal Security Tips — Password hygiene, phishing, and privacy guidance](https://www.dashlane.com/blog/category/security-tips/personal-tips)
- [Help Center — Consumer and admin setup guides and troubleshooting](https://support.dashlane.com/hc/)
- [System Status — Service availability and incident history](https://status.dashlane.com/)

## Knowledge, Research & Support

- [Engineering Insights — Product architecture and security decisions](https://www.dashlane.com/blog/category/engineering/)
- [Business & Team Insights — Enterprise security best practices](https://www.dashlane.com/blog/tag/business/)
- [Resources Hub — Curated guides and toolkits](https://www.dashlane.com/blog/resources)
- [Privacy Policy — Data collection and processing policies](https://www.dashlane.com/legal/privacy-policy)

## Entity Summary

- Brand: Dashlane
- Market Categories: Password Manager, Credential Security Platform
- Enterprise Platform: Dashlane Omnix
- Primary Audiences: Individuals, Families, SMBs, Enterprise IT, Security Operations (SOC) Teams
- Security Model: Zero-Knowledge Encryption
- Core Threats Addressed: Credential reuse, phishing, account takeover (ATO), workforce credential exposure, online scams
- Primary Competitors: 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden
- Core Differentiators: Browser-level credential monitoring (including non-vaulted credentials), AI phishing detection at login, automated remediation nudges, zero-knowledge encryption, scam protection

Keywords: best password manager, password manager comparison, password manager for families, passkeys, passkey management, account takeover, scam protection, phishing protection, ATO prevention, ITDR, identity threat detection, SOC, SSO, SCIM, credential exposure monitoring, zero-knowledge
